text:
maya: Heads-up — after the  PR 3412 merge today we're seeing a ~30% token/sec drop on canary in us-west-2. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/perf/graphs?run=canary-3412 :grimacing:
ci-bot: PERF_CHECK: psutil token_rate drop detected for canary-3412 at 2026-03-18T10:12:34Z (regression compared to baseline)
raj: ugh, that correlates with the continuous-batcher heuristic tweak (auto-shrink threshold). Can you paste the exact commit?
maya: commit 7f9d8a2 — changes to batcher: reduce target batch size when queueing latency > 15ms. Also kernel selection added a fallback heuristic for sequence_len < 64.
andre: I ran a quick perf profile on a repro load (replicated traffic from prod 2026-03-17). Flamegraph shows a spike in GEMM kernel time at step 1 of generation. Probable kernel mismatch.
liz: also noticed KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 68% on the same canary traces. Batches are smaller now so we rebuild KV caches more often.
taylor: smaller batches -> fewer prefix reuse opportunities, yep. That will kill token/sec on long chat sessions.
andre: more detail: the kernel selector is choosing the FP32 fma kernel for certain attention dims when batch_size<4 because our heuristic assumed dense packing. For q4_0 models that's slower than the quantized path — 1.8x slower wall time.
maya: are you saying the selector logic regressed because batcher shrank batches?
andre: it's two-way: batcher change reduced batch sizes which triggered the selector's fallback branch. The selector code was tuned on our old distribution (most requests batched >8). We missed adding a guard for quantized model types.
raj: can we quickly flip selector to prefer quantized kernels for q* models regardless of batch_size? If that's safe it should recover throughput immediately.
liz: second order: the batch-shrink also increased eviction churn in KV cache. If we do the kernel toggle we'll recover some perf but KV hitrate still needs addressing.
sre-bot: ROLL_OUT_BLOCKED: canary-3412 flagged for rollback by SRE on channel eng-runtime due to perf regression.
taylor: I can push a config flag to prefer quant-kernel for q4 models — low risk toggle. Who can validate traces?
andre: I validated locally with the flag — token/sec back up to baseline, latency slightly higher p95 by ~4ms but within SLO.
maya: please open a hotfix PR with the flag and a short description + link to profiler. Tag me and @raj.
raj: I'll start a bisect too to see whether we can revert just the batcher heuristic vs revert the whole merge. Bisect plan: isolate commit in PR 3412 that changed batch shrink code.
ci-bot: PERF_BISECT: scheduled bisect job for canary-3412. Results ETA ~ 18m.
liz: parallel task: I'm adding an experiment to KV cache to prevent prefix eviction when recent reuse > 1s. That should stabilize hitrate while we decide on batcher change.
maya: action items: (1) andre -> hotfix kernel-pref flag PR (2) raj -> bisect to isolate batcher sub-change (3) liz -> KV cache quick-patch experiment (4) taylor -> prepare rollback plan if bisect indicates batcher is root cause.
andre: starting PR now (will link once created).
raj: starting bisect job. If bisect points to batcher we should revert that single file first.
maya: thanks all. Please post updates here. If CI bisect or hotfix shows stable recovery we'll proceed to un-block rollout. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: PERF_BISECT_RESULT: preliminary indicates regression aligns with commit 7f9d8a2 (batcher shrink heuristic). Full run ongoing.
andy: (note) we should add a unit test that simulates low-latency distribution and ensures kernel selector picks quant path for quantized model types — prevents future regressions.
maya: agreed, add test to selector suite. Closing loop once hotfix is merged and canary shows recovery.
ci-bot: HOTFIX_PR: link https://redwood.internal/pull/3478 (andre) — pref-qk flag for q4 models. 
andre: PR merged and rolled to canary at 2026-03-18T10:42:01Z — monitoring.
ci-bot: METRICS: token/sec back to 98% of baseline after hotfix roll (10m window). KV hitrate still ~72%.
liz: KV task still ongoing. If kv patch stabilizes hitrate we'll re-run canary with the new batcher config (tweak threshold) to try to regain some latency improvements without killing throughput.
maya: great. filing follow-up doc in eng-runtime triage. Thanks everyone.
